correctness.rationale: If hub absent, each blade must be represented for domination and selected subgraph is a disjoint union of cliques: perfect matching iff every blade selected count is positive even. With hub selected, domination is automatic and matching the hub to exactly one blade forces precisely that blade odd, all others even; conversely such parity permits internal matchings. Binomial parity subpolynomials E_m and O_m enumerate disjoint cases; x=1 yields exact total, coefficient x² is km and no 0- or 1-member paired domination exists. Independent brute-force domination, exact perfect matching recursion, and polynomial coefficients agree for six parameter pairs (k,m)=(2,2),(2,3),(2,4),(3,2),(3,3),(4,2) including first boundary cases.

value.rationale: A complete coefficient enumerator is a natural established graph invariant, not a contrived parameter slice. It refines the known paired-domination minimum to every feasible cardinality and makes the exact incidence of center and peripheral clique selections transparent for an infinite family; an exact benchmark for paired-domination polynomial questions. The proof is elementary but the full natural unknown invariant remains useful.

final_claim: For generalized windmill graphs W_(k,m)=K1 join kK_m with k,m>=2, paired-dominating sets have exactly one odd selected blade when the hub is present, or positive even selections in every blade when hub absent, yielding polynomial k*x*O_m(x)*E_m(x)^(k-1)+(E_m(x)-1)^k with total k*2^(k(m-1))+(2^(m-1)-1)^k and km minimum sets.
